excerpt: if being F grounds being G, our account implies that being G just is being F or H for some given H, and which on our account gives the (or a) full essence of being G. It then follows that necessarily, a thing is G iff it is F or H, which entails by straightforward modal reasoning that necessarily, a thing is F only if it’s also G, as desired.
overview: This passage connects the grounding analysis back to essence. It shows that the necessity linking a ground to what it grounds is not imposed as an isolated modal principle; it is derived from what the grounded phenomenon is, according to the generalized-identity account.
title: Grounding Necessitation Derivation
